case_name: T. N. Godavarman Thirumulkpad v Union of India and Others
facts: The case involves the protection and conservation of forests throughout the country.
Notice was issued to all Central Government agencies and State Governments.
The Court heard arguments from various counsel, including the Attorney General for India and learned counsel appearing for the States and parties/applicants.
The Court deferred further hearing to enable counsel to study certain points.
Interim directions were necessary at this stage in respect of some aspects.
issues: The scope of the Forest Conservation Act, 1980
The meaning of the word 'forest' used therein
The need for prior approval of the Central Government for certain activities in forest areas
court_reasoning: The Forest Conservation Act, 1980 was enacted to check further deforestation and ecological imbalance.
Prior approval of the Central Government is required for any non-forest activity within a forest area.
All on-going activities in forests must cease forthwith without prior approval.
A complete ban on felling of trees in certain areas is necessary to maintain ecological balance.
holding: The Court directs that all saw mills, veneer and plywood mills in certain areas be closed immediately.
The felling of trees in all forests is to remain suspended except in accordance with the Working Plans of the State Governments.
A complete ban on the movement of cut trees and timber from certain states to other states is necessary.
Each State Government must constitute an Expert Committee to identify areas which are 'forests' or were earlier forests but stand degraded, denuded or cleared.
